    系列：Fund Strategy

    Bond funds in a bull market

    August 7, 2026
    Figure: Bond funds (especially quality bond funds) rise steadily long-term; in a bull they rarely correct, so the tactic can be more "aggressive" — a one-shot buy.

    How to invest in bond funds during a bull market?

    Why one-shot buying in a bull market

    For bond funds in a bull market we take a one-shot buy — why?

    1. Bond funds basically keep rising through a bull market; quality bond funds are themselves long-term risers;
    2. Quality bond funds are positive ~75% of the time, and in a bull market a pullback is unlikely.

    So we can be a bit more aggressive — we only need its performance to be below the historical average, and we buy in one shot.

    Because in a bull market funds usually outperform, what we earn is the income from returning to normal returns through to the excess-return stage.

    Figure: A bond fund in a bull mostly sits above its historical monthly-average return line; when it dips below (current return under the historical average), buy in one shot.

    Specific buy conditions

    ① First tally the bond fund’s historical average monthly return, historical max monthly return, and historical average annualised return; ② When current return is below the historical average monthly return, we can buy in one shot.

    Specific sell conditions

    Figure: Bond bull sells in three tranches — sell 1/3 when YTD return passes the average annualised, another 1/3 at the (max+avg) midpoint, and clear when it reaches 90% of the historical max annualised.

    ① When year-to-date return > historical average annualised return, sell 1/3; ② When year-to-date return > the midpoint between the historical max and average annualised return, sell 1/3; ③ When year-to-date return > 90% of the historical maximum return, clear the position.

    The reason for clearing is, as always, to respect history and patterns, and give up fantasy and luck.
